subject: Deployment-mode decision: latency & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Alex Barnes <alex@fastretail.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: deployment mode discussion & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Key constraints you mentioned:
- Latency SLO: p95 inference latency <= 120ms for ~512 token responses during peak events.
- Throughput: expected concurrent peak ~600–900 qps for short bursts (holiday promos).
- Data residency: US-only; no cross-region failover without approval.
- Cost sensitivity: want to balance predictable cost vs performance—latency is the higher priority.

Path options we discussed (high level):
1) Hosted API (Redwood managed): fastest to onboard, pay-as-you-go, supports burst via autoscaling. Best for initial lift-and-shift and short pilots; may require aggressive caching/quantization for p95 <= 120ms at high qps.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput with isolation. Best fit when latency is primary and predictable peak throughput is needed—recommended for sustained >500 qps peaks.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem): for strict compliance and full control—likely later phase given procurement timeline.

What we need from you to size a recommended Dedicated pool vs Hosted profile: 
- Confirm whether p95 latency target (120ms) is firm or a target range (e.g., 120–180ms).
- Example request/response size distribution (avg tokens in/out). If you can share a short CSV or representative sample, that helps.
- Target pilot window and approval owners for the SOW (procurement contact copied).

Suggested immediate next steps (proposed by Redwood):
- You OK with a Dedicated pilot (2 weeks) to validate p95 at realistic traffic? If yes, we prepare a pilot SOW and a simple runbook.
- If you prefer Hosted first, we can run a 7–10 day stress test using our hosted pool + prefix cache to measure p95 and recommend next actions.

I attached a lightweight sizing-template (fastretail-sizing-template.xlsx) that captures token distribution and peak patterns if helpful.

Can you confirm preference (Dedicated pilot vs Hosted stress test) and whether Sarah should be the procurement approver on the SOW?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the pilot materials once you confirm.

Best,

Alex —

Quick technical notes based on the targets you confirmed (p95 <= 120ms, spikes to ~800 qps):

Recommended Dedicated pilot configuration (conservative):
- 4x NVIDIA A10G / equivalent (reserved pool) with shard-aware routing. Expected sustained p95 for 512-token outputs: ~70–110ms depending on input token variance. Handles steady 150 qps and bursts to ~800 qps with autoscale headroom if you allow a small burst pool.
- If you need very tight p95 headroom for 512 tokens under full burst without any caching, we recommend 6x A10G or 4x A100 for additional single-request latency improvement.

Hosted (managed) approach tradeoffs:
- Pros: Faster onboarding, pay-as-you-go, no infra ops. With aggressive prefix caching and quantization we can often hit p95 ~120–160ms at high qps for many workloads, but it’s workload-dependent.
- Cons: Less predictable cost at extreme peaks and multi-tenant noisy-neighbor risk (mitigated by our burst policies and smart routing).

Pilot proposal (recommended):
1) 2-week Dedicated pilot on 4x A10G configured for your US region. Redwood provides test harness + synthetic replay (you provide 24hr sample) to validate p95 at real traffic shape.
2) Parallel Hosted stress test (optional) to compare cost/latency delta with same sample.
3) Deliverables: latency/throughput report, cost estimate for 99th percentile of expected monthly token volume, runbook for cutover and rollback.

Estimated order-of-magnitude monthly cost (ballpark for procurement):
- Hosted stress approach: ~$12k–$25k/mo depending on tokens and caching effectiveness.
- Dedicated 4x A10G reserved pool (monthly commit): ~$38k–$55k/mo depending on region and GPU SKU.

I will attach a short estimate PDF and the pilot runbook link for procurement and engineering to review. Let me know if you want a configuration using A100s instead — we can price that.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
